title: Company-wide policies and processes — consolidated reference
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose
This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and process references for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the internal templates used to execute those processes. It is intended as the canonical internal reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and long-term vendors that interact with Redwood systems or handle company data.
- Operational owners listed below are responsible for maintaining the sections relevant to their teams.

Primary owners and contacts
- People Ops (policy owner): Maya Thompson (people-ops@redwood.com)
- Security (controls & reviews): Elena Park (security@redwood.com)
- Finance & Procurement: Jordan Li (finance@redwood.com)
- IT / Eng Infra (access provisioning): Samir Rao (eng-infra@redwood.com)

1) Access & permissions
Goal: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent approval workflows, and auditable provisioning for all systems.

Key principles
- Principle of Least Privilege: access is granted only for the duration and scope necessary to perform job duties.
- Role-based provisioning where possible (RBAC).
- Time-bound access for contractors and temporary projects.
- Approval & audit trail preserved for every access change.

Process: Request -> Approve -> Provision -> Audit
1. Request
   - Employee submits an Access Request using the internal Access Request template (link in Templates section). Include justification, resource names, required duration, and approver(s).
2. Approval
   - Manager approval required for any new access. For sensitive systems (prod, key management, customer data stores) security review and second-level approver required.
   - Approval thresholds:
     - Low-risk (read-only non-prod): manager
     - Medium-risk (write non-prod, read prod logs): manager + team security delegate
     - High-risk (prod write, KMS/HSM, PII): manager + security + eng-infra lead
3. Provisioning
   - Eng Infra/IT provisions via IAM or ticketing system (ServiceNow/Jira). Use standardized roles when available. Document any custom role mappings.
4. Review & Audit
   - Quarterly access recertification for high-risk systems. Ad-hoc audits when system owners detect unusual activity.

Role -> Typical permissions (examples)
| Role | Typical systems | Typical permissions | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Developer (non-prod) | dev clusters, staging services | Read/Write non-prod, no prod access | Eng teams
| Platform Engineer | infra, CI/CD, monitoring | Admin on infra services, limited prod deploys | Eng Infra
| Support Engineer | support tools, logs | Read prod logs, no configuration changes | Customer Success / Eng
| Security Analyst | SIEM, audit logs | Read/Investigate, can request escalations | Security

Emergency access
- For emergency mitigation, owners may request break-glass access via PagerDuty/Incident channel. All emergency access must be documented within 24 hours and reviewed by Security and People Ops.

2) Change management
Goal: Reduce risk from configuration and software changes while enabling fast, predictable delivery.

Change types
- Standard Change: Low-risk, pre-authorized changes (routine maintenance, certificate renewals).
- Normal Change: Requires change request, review, and scheduled window (feature releases, infra changes).
- Emergency Change: Immediate changes to restore service or mitigate security issues.

Change advisory process
1. Submit change request in Jira using the Change Request template. Include scope, rollback plan, test plan, owner, and scheduled window.
2. Review:
   - Standard: change owner + automation lead sign-off.
   - Normal: CAB review (weekly) for cross-team impact; security and SRE must review for prod-impacting changes.
   - Emergency: post-facto CAB review; must document timeline, risk, and residual actions.
3. Deployment checklist (must be completed prior to rollout):
   - Backout plan documented
   - Automated tests and canary plan defined
   - Monitoring and alerting configured for the change window
   - Stakeholders notified (oncall, product, CS)

SLOs for change process
- Normal changes: 95% of change requests reviewed by CAB within 3 business days.
- Emergency reviews: post-change documentation within 24 hours.

Rollback and postmortem
- Any change causing SEV impact must be rolled back and followed by a postmortem within 5 business days. Owner responsible for action items and closure.

3) Data management
Goal: Protect data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while retaining necessary records for business and compliance.

Data classification
- Public: information safe for external distribution (marketing collateral).
- Internal: non-sensitive operational data (internal docs, wikis).
- Confidential: PII, customer data, financials, model training data with restrictions.
- Restricted: encryption keys, credentials, customer-protected data under contract.

Handling rules (by class)
- Public: no special handling.
- Internal: stored on internal systems with basic access control.
- Confidential: encrypted at rest and in transit; access logged and limited to approved roles.
- Restricted: multi-factor access, HSM/KMS for key material; periodic revalidation.

Retention and deletion
- Minimum retention follows legal/contractual requirements. Data owners must publish retention schedules.
- Deletion procedure: documented request -> verification by data owner -> secure deletion (wipe/crypto-delete) -> audit record.

Backups and DR
- Critical data (customer data, critical configs) backed up daily with 30/90-day retention depending on classification.
- Disaster Recovery drills annually; restore targets: RPO <= 1 hour for critical production state, RTO <= 4 hours for core services.

Data access reviews
- Quarterly reviews for Confidential/Restricted data sets. Findings escalated to Security and People Ops.

4) Procurement & expenses
Goal: Ensure compliant, cost-effective procurement and timely reimbursement.

Procurement thresholds
- Purchases < $2,000: Manager-level approval.
- $2,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- > $25,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement lead; require vendor contract review.

Preferred vendors and cloud marketplaces
- Use approved vendor list maintained by Finance (link in related pages). Cloud marketplace purchases should be routed through corporate cloud billing accounts unless pre-approved.

Procurement process (high-level)
1. Create Purchase Request (PR) in procurement system with business justification, vendor, and cost estimate.
2. Finance reviews budget impact and compliance.
3. Procurement negotiates contract terms and issues PO.
4. Receiving & invoice: validate goods/services, then Finance processes payment.

Expense reimbursement
- Use the company expense system (Concur/Expensify) and submit receipts within 30 days.
- Per diem and travel limits: see Travel Policies section.
- Non-compliant expenses (personal items, lavish entertainment) will be rejected.

5) Vendor management
Goal: Maintain a consistent vendor onboarding and lifecycle program that ensures security, financial, and contractual risk are managed.

Onboarding checklist
- Complete Vendor Intake form (includes scope, data access needs, contract owner).
- Security questionnaire and risk scoring performed by Security.
- Contract reviewed by Finance/Legal for terms on data residency, liability, and SLAs.
- Finance sets up payment terms and PO if required.
- Technical onboarding: scoped least-privilege access, monitoring hooks (if applicable), and escalation contacts.

Vendor risk tiers and controls
- Tier 1 (High): vendors with access to customer data or production systems — require SOC2/ISO audit evidence and are subject to quarterly reviews.
- Tier 2 (Medium): vendors with internal data access — require security questionnaire and annual attestations.
- Tier 3 (Low): SaaS with no data access — minimal review and record in vendor registry.

Offboarding
- Revoke access, ensure return/destruction of data, confirm final invoices, and update vendor registry. Offboarding checklist must be completed within 5 business days of contract termination.

6) Travel policy (business travel & expenses)
Goal: Provide clear expectations for booking, approvals, and reimbursement while maintaining cost controls.

Booking & approvals
- Domestic travel: manager approval required for trips >$500 or overnight stays.
- International travel: manager + people-ops approval; travel risk assessment required for high-risk countries.
- Preferred booking: corporate travel portal for flights and hotels. Use lowest logical fare with reasonable schedule.

Per diem & reimbursements
- Meals: up to $75/day US (regional variations apply; check local policy).
- Ground transportation: rideshare or reasonable taxi; use receipts for reimbursements.
- Lodging: reasonable, mid-tier business hotels; economy upgrades covered only with manager pre-approval.

Safety & insurance
- All business travelers covered by company travel insurance. Emergency contact details must be provided prior to international trips.

7) Internal templates and examples
The following templates are maintained centrally in the Templates library (link). Copy and populate these for all requests to avoid delays.
- Access Request template: required fields: requester, resource(s) requested, justification, duration, manager approver, security reviewer (if applicable).
- Change Request template: required fields: owner, scope, rollback plan, test/canary plan, notification list, scheduled window.
- Vendor Intake / Risk template: vendor name, contact, scope, data access required, security questionnaire link, contract owner.
- Expense Report template: trip dates, purpose, itemized expenses with receipts, manager approval line.

Examples (short)
Access Request (example)
Requester: John Doe
Resource: prod-s3-billing-logs
Justification: Investigating billing discrepancy for customer X
Duration: 48 hours
Approver: Manager, Security

Change Request (example)
Owner: Platform Team
Change: Upgrade load balancer kernel parameter to fix connection drops
Rollback: Revert kernel parameter using config-management to previous value
Canary: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes

Governance and maintenance
- Policy review cadence: Annual review by People Ops with reviewers from Security, Finance, and Eng Infra.
- Ad-hoc updates may be issued when legal/regulatory changes occur.

How to get help
- For policy clarifications: people-ops@redwood.com
- For urgent access issues: eng-infra oncall (PagerDuty)
- For security reviews or incidents: security@redwood.com

Revision history

- 2026-06-15: Added emergency access break-glass workflow (Security).
- 2026-11-22: Updated procurement thresholds and vendor tiering (Finance).

Appendix: Quick checklists (copy these into request forms)
Access request quick checklist:
- [ ] Requester and manager fields filled
- [ ] Justification provided and time-bound
- [ ] Security reviewer assigned if required
- [ ] Provisioning ticket created

Change request quick checklist:
- [ ] Rollback plan attached
- [ ] Monitoring setup for canary
- [ ] Stakeholders notified

Procurement quick checklist:
- [ ] Budget approval obtained
- [ ] Vendor on approved list or contract reviewed
- [ ] PO or contract in place before payment

End of document
